blocker: The residue and its software-visible effect are proven, but the stronger integrity claim was not demonstrated in simulation. The residual pcr_hash_extend_ip forces the key-vault write enable to 1 at sha512.sv:470 and replaces the destination entry with the surviving hash_extend_entry at sha512.sv:471, which would mean a security erase leaves the block's vault write path armed at an attacker-chosen entry. Showing that as an actual unauthorised write needs a modelled PCR/key-vault fabric that answers the write handshake, and this testbench deliberately holds those response ports quiescent, because doing so is also what keeps kv_dest_done from retiring the bit. What is measured here is therefore the availability half: the PCR hash extend engine is permanently unavailable to software after the erase. The integrity half is reported as a structural consequence with its RTL lines named, not as an observed write.
proof_method_executed: Thirty-two scripted structural gates over the submitted checkout, a directed VCS W-2024.09-SP1 simulation of one unmodified sha512 elaborated through the project's own src/sha512/config/sha512_ctrl.vf filelist and driven only over its register bus, and a negative control that adds the two missing clears to a scratch copy of sha512.sv and re-runs the identical testbench.
result_summary: One sha512 was driven through its register bus only, with offsets taken from the generated header. In the quiescent state SHA512_GEN_PCR_HASH_STATUS.READY read as ready, and it still read ready after a bare ZEROIZE with no extend in progress, which rules out the erase stalling the PCR path by itself. A PCR hash extend was then started by writing SHA512_VAULT_RD_CTRL with read_en, pcr_hash_extend and read_entry 7, and the status went not-ready, confirming pcr_hash_extend_ip was set. ZEROIZE was then written while the extend was still in flight. The status remained not-ready, while SHA512_STATUS.READY read high in the same window, so the block itself had recovered from the erase and only the PCR extend path was stuck. After 200 further idle cycles with the vault interfaces quiescent the status was still not-ready, and no register-bus error was raised anywhere in the run.
security_impact_assessment: Availability of a security-critical engine, plus a defence-in-depth failure of the block's erase path. After the sequence above, software cannot start another PCR hash extend: sha512.sv:335 holds SHA512_GEN_PCR_HASH_STATUS.READY low while pcr_hash_extend_ip is set, and the only non-reset clear at sha512.sv:372 requires pcr_hash_extend_ip & kv_dest_done, a vault completion for the very transaction the zeroize cancelled. The residue therefore cannot retire and the engine stays unavailable until a reset. The erase-hygiene failure is broader than the stall: the same bit forces the key-vault write enable high at sha512.sv:470 and substitutes the surviving hash_extend_entry as the write destination at sha512.sv:471, so operation-specific routing chosen before the erase outlives it. That direction is not claimed as demonstrated. Notably, zeroize_reg is raised not only by SHA512_CTRL.ZEROIZE but also by debugUnlock_or_scan_mode_switch at sha512.sv:284-286, so the same incomplete erase sits on a debug and scan-mode boundary.

evidence.key_observation: On the unmodified tree: baseline_gen_ready=1, gen_ready_after_bare_zeroize=1, gen_ready_during_extend=0, gen_ready_after_zeroize=0, core_ready_after_zeroize=1, gen_ready_after_idle=0. The PCR hash status reads ready in the clean state and after a bare erase, but stays not-ready after an erase issued mid-extend, while the block's own readiness is high in that same window. Verdict line SUMMARY checks=7 fails=1 witness_hits=2 with cov_extend_set=1, cov_ip_survives=1, cov_core_ready=1, cov_no_extend_no_stall=1.
evidence.negative_evidence: With the mitigation applied to a scratch copy, adding pcr_hash_extend_ip <= '0 and hash_extend_entry <= '0 to the zeroize branch, the same testbench measured gen_ready_after_zeroize=1, the witness stopped reproducing, and PROOF_RESULT went to FAIL, while the quiescent baseline and the no-bus-error containment were unchanged and the extend was still confirmed to have taken effect before the erase. That run is also the positive evidence that the erase was firing at all in the audited run: the only edit was inside the zeroize branch, so the changed outcome can only come from that branch being taken.

evidence_items: src/sha512/rtl/sha512.sv:217-227 is the asynchronous reset branch, and it clears pcr_hash_extend_ip at line 224 and hash_extend_entry at line 225, which establishes both as state the module treats as reset-worthy.

src/sha512/rtl/sha512.sv:229-238 is the zeroize branch. It performs exactly eight assignments and neither register appears among them, while digest_reg, kv_reg and pcr_sign_reg do, so the branch is a real erase path rather than a stub.

src/sha512/rtl/sha512.sv:255-257 holds the only other assignments to the two registers, inside the else branch that a zeroize does not take, so the erase neither clears them nor allows their normal update to run. Each register has exactly two assignment sites in the module.
src/sha512/rtl/sha512.sv:335 gates SHA512_GEN_PCR_HASH_STATUS.READY on ~gen_hash_ip & ~pcr_hash_extend_ip & ready_reg, which is what makes the residue visible to software over plain MMIO.

src/sha512/rtl/sha512.sv:372 is the only non-reset clear and reads pcr_hash_extend_ip & kv_dest_done, so retiring the residue requires the vault completion the erase cancelled. This is why the stall is permanent rather than transient.

src/sha512/rtl/sha512.sv:459-462 gates all four pv_write fields on the bit, src/sha512/rtl/sha512.sv:470 forces the key-vault write enable to 1 while it is set, and src/sha512/rtl/sha512.sv:471 substitutes hash_extend_entry as the write destination.

src/sha512/rtl/sha512.sv:284-286 shows zeroize_reg is raised by SHA512_CTRL.ZEROIZE or debugUnlock_or_scan_mode_switch, and src/sha512/rtl/sha512.sv:192 shows the same zeroize_reg is what erases the SHA-512 core itself, so this is the block's main erase signal.

src/sha512/rtl/sha512.sv:371 sets the bit from kv_read_ctrl_reg.read_en & kv_read_ctrl_reg.pcr_hash_extend, both software-writable fields of SHA512_VAULT_RD_CTRL at 0x10020600, bit 6 being pcr_hash_extend and read_entry starting at bit 1.
non_findings: This is not a demonstrated key-vault or PCR write. The vault response ports are held quiescent by construction, so the forced write enable and overridden destination entry are reported from the RTL, not from an observed transaction.

This is not a claim about SHA512_DIGEST or about zeroize_reg2. The digest hardware-clear at src/sha512/rtl/sha512.sv:300 is driven from a different signal whose construction is a separate finding, and it is excluded from this case.
This is not a defect in the asynchronous reset path, which clears both registers correctly at src/sha512/rtl/sha512.sv:224-225.
This is not a stall of the SHA-512 block as a whole. SHA512_STATUS.READY reads high after the erase in the witness case, and a bare erase with no extend in progress leaves the PCR hash status ready.

reproduction.tools: VCS W-2024.09-SP1 at /data0/tools/Synopsys/vcs/vcs/W-2024.09-SP1/bin, bash, python3. CALIPTRA_ROOT points at the submitted checkout, CALIPTRA_PRIM_ROOT at src/caliptra_prim_generic, CALIPTRA_PRIM_MODULE_PREFIX is caliptra_prim_generic.
reproduction.success_marker: PROOF_RESULT: PASS from the simulation script, result=PASS with structural_gates_passed=32/32 from the structural audit, NEGATIVE_CONTROL: PASS from the negative control.
reproduction.determinism: Fully deterministic. The stimulus is a fixed directed register-bus sequence with no randomization and no seed dependence. Bus transactions are driven from a single task that waits for the handshake rather than counting cycles, so no measurement depends on event ordering within a time slot.
reproduction.note_on_verdict_markers: The testbench prints result=PASS only on success. Its failure branch prints PROOF_RESULT: FAIL with no result= line, because the negative control run is supposed to reach that branch and a bare result=FAIL would be read as a real failure by the log scanners.
reproduction.note_on_filelist: The simulation script expands src/sha512/config/sha512_ctrl.vf with two adjustments that change neither the set of files compiled nor their contents: it appends an include path for the generated register headers, which files reachable from that list require but which the list does not carry, and it emits packages ahead of modules because the list places some modules before the packages they import.
reproduction.note_on_log_order: The negative control invokes the simulation script with a DUT override, so it overwrites run.log and witness.log. The unmodified-tree simulation is re-run last so the submitted logs describe the audited RTL, with the negative control's own output preserved in negative_control.log.

conclusion: The defect is confirmed and reproducible: the zeroize branch of sha512's reg_update block omits pcr_hash_extend_ip and hash_extend_entry, which the asynchronous reset branch two branches above does clear, so a security erase issued during a PCR hash extend leaves the extend routing state set. Because the only non-reset clear needs the vault completion that the same erase cancelled, the residue cannot retire, and software sees SHA512_GEN_PCR_HASH_STATUS.READY stuck low while the block otherwise reports itself ready. Adding the two clears flips the measurement, which establishes non-vacuity. It is filed as partial_proof because the availability effect was measured end to end over the register bus while the integrity direction, an erase leaving the vault write path armed at an attacker-chosen entry, rests on the RTL at sha512.sv:470-471 and was not exercised against a modelled vault.
